Adversarially verify ONE candidate security finding in /srv/skytec/metacritic-ai-watch. Read the code; do not modify files.

CANDIDATE: Unvalidated URL scheme in rendered links — stored XSS via javascript: URLs.
Locations: app/templates/game.html href="{{ game.video_url }}" (~line 25), href="{{ lp.url }}" (~lines 104, 112), and app/templates/_macros.html src="{{ src }}" (~line 19-21).
Claim: these URLs come from upstream (Metacritic Nuxt payload / JSON-LD trailer via app/scraper/metacritic.py _video_url and _cover_url; yt-dlp search entry via app/youtube.py search_letsplay). Jinja autoescaping prevents quote-breakout but not a `javascript:` or `data:` scheme. Values are persisted in the DB and served to all visitors, so a hostile upstream value yields stored XSS when a visitor clicks.
Claimed severity: Low. Claimed confidence 0.7.

FALSE POSITIVE FILTERING - Automatically EXCLUDE:
1. DoS / resource exhaustion. 2. Secrets on disk. 3. Rate limiting. 4. Memory/CPU exhaustion. 5. Lack of input validation on non-security-critical fields WITHOUT proven security impact. 6. GH Actions. 7. Lack of hardening measures — only concrete vulnerabilities. 8. Theoretical race conditions. 9. Outdated libraries. 10. Memory safety in safe languages. 11. Test-only files. 12. Log spoofing. 13. SSRF controlling only path. 14. User content in AI prompts. 15. Regex injection. 16. Regex DoS. 17. Documentation. 18. Audit logs.

PRECEDENTS: Subtle/low-impact web vulnerabilities should not be reported unless EXTREMELY high confidence.

CRITICAL for this one: assess how realistic the threat model is. The data source is metacritic.com and YouTube via yt-dlp — trusted-ish third parties, not arbitrary attackers. Ask: can a genuine ATTACKER (not just "a hypothetical upstream change") actually control video_url or lp.url? Investigate: (a) does Metacritic let users submit trailer/video URLs or any field flowing into _video_url? (b) can a YouTube uploader influence the `url` field returned by yt-dlp's flat search extractor, or is it always reconstructed as a youtube.com/watch?v=<id> URL? Read app/youtube.py search_letsplay and app/scraper/metacritic.py _video_url/_cover_url closely. If no attacker-controlled path exists, this is defense-in-depth (exclusion 7). Note also whether MITM is relevant (are these fetched over https?).

Output: verdict (REAL / FALSE POSITIVE / PARTIALLY VALID), confidence 1-10, 4-8 sentences citing exact file:line. Be adversarial and skeptical.

1	"""Let's-play lookup: find the most watched playthrough, read what the blogger says.
2	
3	Search runs through yt-dlp's flat extractor (one request, and it already carries view
4	counts). The spoken text comes from YouTube's own captions; only when there are none
5	do we fall back to downloading the audio and running Whisper locally.
6	
7	Both of those last steps need full video extraction, which YouTube refuses from
8	datacenter IPs ("Sign in to confirm you're not a bot"). Point `YOUTUBE_COOKIES_FILE`
9	at an exported cookie jar to lift that; without it the stage records `none` and the
10	crawl carries on.
11	"""
12	
13	from __future__ import annotations
14	
15	import logging
16	import re
17	import time
18	from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
19	from http.cookiejar import MozillaCookieJar
20	from pathlib import Path
21	
22	from app.config import settings
23	from app.llm import chat_json
24	
25	log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
26	
27	MAX_TRANSCRIPT_CHARS = 12_000
28	TRANSCRIPT_LANGUAGES = ("en", "ru")
29	
30	#: Titles that are clearly not a playthrough.
31	NOT_A_LETSPLAY = re.compile(
32	    r"\b(trailer|teaser|announce\w*|reveal|review|обзор|трейлер|рецензи\w+|"
33	    r"ost|soundtrack|music|подборка|top\s*\d+|все\s+концовки|all\s+endings)\b",
34	    re.IGNORECASE,
35	)
36	_WORD_RE = re.compile(r"[a-zа-яё0-9]+", re.IGNORECASE)
37	
38	
39	class YouTubeError(RuntimeError):
40	    pass
41	
42	
43	@dataclass
44	class Video:
45	    video_id: str
46	    url: str
47	    title: str
48	    channel: str | None
49	    view_count: int
50	    duration: int
51	
52	    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
53	        return asdict(self)
54	
55	
56	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------- search
57	
58	
59	def _title_words(title: str) -> set[str]:
60	    """Distinctive words of a game title — short ones match everything."""
61	    return {w.lower() for w in _WORD_RE.findall(title) if len(w) > 2}
62	
63	
64	def is_letsplay(entry: dict, game_title: str) -> bool:
65	    """Long enough, about this game, and not a trailer or a review."""
66	    if (entry.get("duration") or 0) < settings.youtube_min_duration:
67	        return False
68	    title = entry.get("title") or ""
69	    if NOT_A_LETSPLAY.search(title):
70	        return False
71	    wanted = _title_words(game_title)
72	    if not wanted:
73	        return False
74	    haystack = _title_words(f"{title} {entry.get('description') or ''}")
75	    # Most of the title has to show up; sequels and subtitles get dropped otherwise.
76	    return len(wanted & haystack) / len(wanted) >= 0.6
77

79	def _ytsearch(query: str) -> list[dict]:
80	    import yt_dlp
81	
82	    options = {
83	        "quiet": True,
84	        "no_warnings": True,
85	        "skip_download": True,
86	        "extract_flat": True,
87	        "noprogress": True,
88	        "socket_timeout": 20,
89	    }
90	    if settings.youtube_cookies_file:
91	        options["cookiefile"] = settings.youtube_cookies_file
92	    with yt_dlp.YoutubeDL(options) as ydl:
93	        result = ydl.extract_info(query, download=False) or {}
94	    return [e for e in (result.get("entries") or []) if isinstance(e, dict)]

98	    """Most watched playthrough of the game, or None if the search finds nothing."""

"""Local cache of game cover art.

Metacritic serves the originals fine, but hotlinking them from our own pages is both
rude and fragile, so a crawl copies each cover into `data/covers/<slug>.<ext>` and the
site serves it from there.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import re
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from pathlib import Path

from app.config import settings
from app.scraper.http import PoliteClient, default_client

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

MAX_BYTES = 5 * 1024 * 1024
MAX_AGE = timedelta(days=30)

EXTENSIONS = {
    "image/jpeg": ".jpg",
    "image/pjpeg": ".jpg",
    "image/png": ".png",
    "image/webp": ".webp",
    "image/gif": ".gif",
    "image/avif": ".avif",
}

#: Leading bytes -> extension. Metacritic mislabels some covers (a PNG served as
#: image/jpeg), so the file itself decides, not the header.
MAGIC = (
    (b"\xff\xd8\xff", ".jpg"),
    (b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n", ".png"),
    (b"GIF87a", ".gif"),
    (b"GIF89a", ".gif"),
)

#: Legacy rows hold a signed `/a/img/resize/<hash>/…` URL that now answers 403.
_SIGNED_RE = re.compile(r"(/a/img/)resize/[0-9a-f]+/")

#: Cache file names are `<slug>.<ext>` and nothing else — the serving route rejects
#: everything that does not match, so no request can escape the directory.
NAME_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,199}\.(jpg|png|webp|gif|avif)$")


def sniff_extension(body: bytes, content_type: str) -> str | None:
    """Extension for the image, from its magic bytes; the header is only a fallback."""
    for prefix, extension in MAGIC:
        if body.startswith(prefix):
            return extension
    if body[:4] == b"RIFF" and body[8:12] == b"WEBP":
        return ".webp"
    if body[4:12] == b"ftypavif":
        return ".avif"
    return EXTENSIONS.get(content_type)


def unsigned_url(url: str | None) -> str | None:
    """Rewrite a signed Metacritic image URL to the unsigned original, and drop the
    resize query string that went with it."""
    if not url:
        return url
    return _SIGNED_RE.sub(r"\1", url.split("?", 1)[0])


def covers_dir() -> Path:
    return settings.data_dir / "covers"


def stored_name(slug: str) -> str | None:
    """File name already cached for this slug, if any."""
    for extension in dict.fromkeys(EXTENSIONS.values()):
        if (covers_dir() / f"{slug}{extension}").exists():
            return f"{slug}{extension}"
    return None


def path_for(name: str) -> Path | None:
    """Validated path for a request to `/covers/<name>`, or None if it is not ours."""
    if not NAME_RE.match(name):
        return None
    path = covers_dir() / name
    return path if path.is_file() else None


def is_fresh(name: str) -> bool:
    path = covers_dir() / name
    if not path.is_file():
        return False
    age = datetime.now(UTC) - datetime.fromtimestamp(path.stat().st_mtime, UTC)
    return age < MAX_AGE


def cache_cover(
    slug: str, url: str | None, client: PoliteClient | None = None, force: bool = False
) -> str | None:
    """Download the cover unless a fresh copy is on disk. Returns the file name."""
    existing = stored_name(slug)
    if existing and not force and is_fresh(existing):
        return existing
    if not url:
        return existing

    try:
        response = (client or default_client()).get(url)
    except Exception as exc:
        # Any failure here — 403, timeout, DNS — is cosmetic. It must never take a
        # crawl down with it, so nothing escapes.
        log.warning("cover download failed for %s: %s", slug, exc)
        return existing

    # Trust the advertised length to bail out early, then check what actually arrived.
    declared = response.headers.get("content-length")
    if declared and declared.isdigit() and int(declared) > MAX_BYTES:
        log.warning("cover for %s is %s bytes, over the limit", slug, declared)
        return existing
    body = response.content
    if len(body) > MAX_BYTES:
        log.warning("cover for %s is %d bytes, over the limit", slug, len(body))
        return existing

    content_type = (response.headers.get("content-type") or "").split(";")[0].strip().lower()
    extension = sniff_extension(body, content_type)
    if extension is None:
        log.warning("cover for %s is not an image (%s)", slug, content_type or "no type")
        return existing

    directory = covers_dir()
    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    name = f"{slug}{extension}"
    # Write beside the target and rename, so a half-written file is never served.
    temporary = directory / f".{name}.part"
    temporary.write_bytes(body)
    temporary.replace(directory / name)
    if existing and existing != name:
        (directory / existing).unlink(missing_ok=True)
    log.info("cached cover %s (%d bytes)", name, len(body))
    return name

import time

content.text: ## Verdict: FALSE POSITIVE (defense-in-depth only, exclusion 7) — confidence 9/10 I traced every write path into the three sinks and found no attacker-controlled route. **yt-dlp `url` is not uploader-controllable.** `app/youtube.py:111` does `best.get("url") or f"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={best['id']}"`. The `url` key in a flat-search entry is not passthrough metadata — yt-dlp hardcodes it in `_extract_video`: `.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/yt_dlp/extractor/youtube/_tab.py:113` (`url = f'https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={video_id}'`, with the only alternate branch at line 115 being `.../shorts/{video_id}`). The scheme and host are string literals in yt-dlp; a channel owner cannot inject `javascript:` regardless of what they put in title, description, or channel name. So `lp.url` at `app/templates/game.html:104` and `:112` is structurally safe. **Metacritic's video object is editorial, not user-submitted.** `app/scraper/metacritic.py:209-221` `_video_url` reads `item["video"]["embedUrl"|"url"|"manifestUrl"]` from the Nuxt payload or `json_ld["trailer"]`. Metacritic's user-contribution surface is user reviews (score + prose), which land in the summary text nodes, not in the video object; there is no field a Metacritic account can set that reaches `_video_url`. Note also that `app/templates/game.html:25` only renders the raw `href` when `youtube_embed()` returns `None` (line 24) — for YouTube trailers the value is discarded and the iframe at line 44 uses the regex-reconstructed `https://www.youtube.com/embed/<11-char-id>` from `app/main.py:49-52`, which is itself a safe literal. **The `_macros.html:21` sink is not an XSS sink at all.** It is ``, and the primary branch (`app/templates/_macros.html:19`) is the local `/covers/` path; the fallback `cover_url` is built as `f"{settings.metacritic_base_url}/a/img/..."` at `app/scraper/metacritic.py:198`. Even with full value control, `javascript:` in `` does not execute in any current browser and `data:` image URLs (including SVG loaded via ``) are script-sandboxed. **No injection channel and no MITM.** The only writers of these columns are the crawler (`app/crawler.py:109`, `:115` and the letsplay stage); all HTTP routes in `app/main.py` are read-only except `POST /monitor/run`, which takes no URL input. All fetches go to `https://www.metacritic.com` / `https://backend.metacritic.com` (`app/config.py:25-26`) through `httpx.Client` with default TLS verification (`app/scraper/http.py:44-51`, no `verify=False` anywhere), so a network attacker cannot supply the value either. Templates use Jinja autoescaping with no `|safe` or `Markup` anywhere. A scheme allowlist here would be reasonable hardening, but with no attacker-controlled path this does not meet the bar for a reported vulnerability under the stated precedent on subtle low-impact web issues.
